core.title: Every authored document declares a non-empty identity id and a non-empty currency status
core.given: An authored document in the documentation tree, outside the generated documentation output tree, new or existing
core.when: documentation is planned, written or validated
core.then: Its header declares a non-empty identity id and a non-empty currency status.
prefer: Declare both in the document header, above the first section: the title, the identity id and the currency status.
Prefix the identity id with the area the document lives in, so id and tree agree; readability only, unchecked.
Currency status: current, superseded or historical.
avoid: Declaring only one: an id without status has unknown currency; a status without id is a claim nothing can reference.
Using a path as identity; the declared identity id is the only node identity the documentation graph uses.
Skipping documents that have no header at all; they are violations.

Treating status as making the archive area honest: it cannot say superseded by what; the supersedes edge does, and it is validated by the rule that resolves documentation-graph edges. This rule only provides identity; it does not by itself discharge the archival-currency issue.
unless: Generated documentation output beneath the documentation root, at the location the profile gives; this check never scans it.
core.why: Edges resolve only against declared identity ids, so an undeclared document can be neither referenced nor found missing; the currency status makes current-versus-historical readable.
evidence: The documentation check reports no identity finding for any document in the documentation tree outside the generated documentation output tree.
A reviewer sees a non-empty identity id and a non-empty currency status in the header of each document in the documentation tree.
verification: Scan every document of the markup file kind beneath the documentation root, regardless of whether the file changed, excluding only the generated documentation output tree whose location the profile supplies; this exclusion is owned by this check itself and is distinct from the stack-wide never-scanned list.

A finding when the identity declaration is absent or empty; a finding when the currency status declaration is absent or empty. These are the only findings: the check does not validate the identifier's grammar or format; the identifier grammar from the profile is descriptive data, not a finding source.
A document with no header at all is a violation, not a skip; silence about a document that declares nothing is the failure mode this rule exists to refuse.
Area-prefix/tree agreement of the identity id is NOT enforced; do not report it.
Declared identity ids form the set against which the sibling rule that resolves documentation-graph edges resolves every edge; supersedes edges are validated there, not here.
Severity 2; strict disposition: the check fails on every finding, with no advisory mode and no ratchet baseline.

fires: A planner authors a new document in any area of the documentation tree.
Any existing document in the documentation tree, changed or not, lacks the identity or the currency declaration, or one of them has an empty value.
A document in scope has no header at all.
doesNotFire: Generated documentation output beneath the documentation root.
Files not of the document markup kind.

neutralityNotes: No keys are proposed: vocabulary v3 already carries every key this core needs (roots.docs, roots.generated, suffix.markup, idiom.docs_syntax via its doc_identity_attributes entry, and urn.grammar via a doc_identity entry). The dotted identifier grammar of the document identity id is supplied by urn.grammar#doc_identity as descriptive profile data only: per core verification, the check's only findings are absent-or-empty identity and absent-or-empty status, area-prefix/tree agreement is explicitly unenforced, and no identifier-format finding is introduced, so instantiation is no stronger than Bun. The generated-output exclusion (Bun: docs/dist/**) is owned by this check, so it stays explicit in core verification with its concrete location supplied by roots.generated; roots.excluded is NOT used by this core and keeps its documented stack-wide union meaning, so instantiation reproduces exactly the Bun scan scope (every markup document beneath the documentation root except the generated output tree, unchanged files included). A stack whose markup suffix list is broader than its authored-document kinds must scope the profile accordingly (Bun: suffix.markup = .adoc), otherwise the neutral scan would be wider than Bun's. The sibling rule id (planner.docs.graph-target-resolves), the validator id (docs_capability), the finding ids and the two term labels remain in the Bun realization; the core refers to them generically (the rule that resolves documentation-graph edges, the documentation check). The status vocabulary (current, superseded, historical) and the supersedes-edge concept are treated as documentation-graph conventions and kept neutral.
